candidates.text: In the medical context, the mere use of sex-based language does not sweep a statute within the reach of heightened scrutiny
candidates.speaker: Roberts
phrases: the mere use of sex-based language does not sweep a statute
candidates.reason: States the case's rule on sex classification in the medical context; the Redburn critique of 'double deference' targets it.

candidates.text: The Equal Protection Clause does not resolve these disagreements. Nor does it afford us license to decide them as we see best
candidates.speaker: Roberts
phrases: we leave questions regarding its policy to the people, their elected representatives
candidates.reason: States the rational-basis disposition and democratic-deference theme praised by defenders.

candidates.text: The Court's willingness to do so here does irrevocable damage to the Equal Protection Clause and invites legislatures
candidates.speaker: Sotomayor
candidates.reason: Principal dissent's central charge, echoed by progressive critics.

candidates.text: The Equal Protection Clause does not demand heightened judicial scrutiny of laws that classify based on transgender status
candidates.speaker: Barrett
candidates.reason: Answers the question the majority left open.

candidates.text: This case carries a simple lesson: In politically contentious debates over matters shrouded in scientific uncertainty
